SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C. & S. B. REGISTRY No. S. B. D. 3183. Special Branch Sec. Sworn. c/o 11 / 32. Date January 22, 1932.）

Subject (in full) Y.M.C.A. Social Center
4200 Robison Road
& forwarded by
Made by Supt. Robertson Forwarded by Jno Robertson, Supt.

It would be better for all concerned if this
Social Center did not exist as the facilities it affords to
bone fide workers is doubtless being taken advantage of by
agitators, although observation has so far failed to detect
evidence of communistic activity among the frequenters of
this establishment. A Chinese detective from Pootoo Road
is on duty on the premises practically all the time in
addition to the place being watched by Special Branch
agents.

Jno Robertson
Superintendent

Officer i/c Special Branch.

J.C. (Dyins)
information and form
of return.

Y. M. C. A. Social Center,
4200 Robison Road,
Shanghai,
January 16, 1932.

Dear Sirs:

Allow me to inform you of our position in connection with the strike of the workers in the Japanese cotton and silk factories in our vicinity, so that you may instruct your men accordingly and will not entertain any misunderstanding towards us or our work.

Since the strike began, the workers have approached us time and again for various kinds of help. As our Center is built to meet the needs of the workers in the Western district, and as we advocate the Christian principle of social justice in our daily activities, we cannot shrink from the responsibility of cooperating with the workers in furthering their legitimate aspirations. We have therefore decided to 1. help the workers organize various committees for carrying on the various important tasks during their period of unemployment, 2. help them maintain discipline and order, 3. give them access to our facilities and let them use our premise for registration, consultation and meetings as long as these are not unlawful and are orderly, 4. utilize this opportunity to lead the workers into right channels of thinking and action by conducting for them classes, lectures and entertainment programs, and 5. if necessary secure work and money for them during their period of need.

At the same time, we are anxious to have you understand that we have not and cannot take any responsibility in settling the dispute between the Japanese owners and the workers, as arbitration and conciliation are the proper functions and duties of the Bureau of Social Affairs. We understand that the strike is already under the attention of the said Bureau. Meanwhile we shall do our best to refrain from interfering with either the workers or their factories. All activities are of course conducted under the name and supervision of the workers themselves. We hope very soon some amicable settlement may be reached so that these workers can resume work, and we also hope you will cooperate with us in following the above policy.

Very truly yours,

（签名）

敬启者：

谨此告知我方就附近日本棉纺厂和丝厂工人罢工一事所持之立场，以便贵方据此指示麾下人员，并对本会或本会工作不致产生任何误解。

自罢工开始以来，工人们屡次向我们寻求各种帮助。鉴于本中心旨在满足西区工人的需求，且我们在日常活动中倡导基督教的社会正义原则，我们不能推卸与工人合作以促进其合法诉求的责任。因此，我们决定：1. 帮助工人组织各类委员会，以便在失业期间开展各项重要工作；2. 帮助他们维持纪律和秩序；3. 向他们开放我们的设施，允许他们使用我们的场所进行登记、咨询和开会，前提是这些活动合法且有序；4. 利用这一机会，通过为他们举办课程、讲座和娱乐节目，引导工人走上正确的思想和行动轨道；5. 如有必要，在他们困难时期为他们谋取工作和资金。

同时，我们亟望贵方理解，对于解决日本资方与工人之间的纠纷，我们未曾也無法承担任何责任，因为仲裁和调解是社会局的正当职能和职责。我们获悉，此次罢工已受到该局的关注。在此期间，我们将尽力避免干涉工人或其工厂。所有活动当然均以工人名义并在其监督下进行。我们希望不久能达成某种友好解决方案，使这些工人能够复工，我们也希望贵方能配合我们执行上述政策。

此致

敬礼

（签名）
